failure_modes.mode: BPR Valve Blockage due to Precipitation
failure_modes.cause: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution products or unreacted solids precipitate in the high-pressure restriction zone, causing pressure spike or flow stoppage.
failure_modes.mitigation: Install inline filter (50 µm) before BPR; implement automated pressure alarm with immediate pump shutdown if dP > 1.5x setpoint.

failure_modes.mode: Loss of Selectivity due to Mixing Inhomogeneity
failure_modes.cause: At Re=16 (laminar flow), insufficient radial mixing leads to concentration gradients, favoring over-substitution or side reactions despite long residence time.
failure_modes.mitigation: Validate mixing efficiency using a fast clock reaction (e.g., iodine clock) at Q=0.56 mL/min; consider static mixer insertion if conversion/selectivity deviates >5% from model.

failure_modes.cause: Operating at 60°C with industrial solvent (likely volatile) near its vapor pressure; if BPR fails or drops below vapor pressure, solvent flashes, causing pump cavitation and pressure loss.
failure_modes.mitigation: Increase BPR setpoint to 2.0 bar (as recommended in safety assessment) to ensure >0.5 bar margin above solvent vapor pressure at 60°C.

single_points_of_failure: BPR Valve — blockage or failure stops all flow and may cause overpressure upstream
Pump Head — failure leads to loss of residence time control and potential thermal runaway if reaction is exothermic
validation_experiments: Run 10-hour continuous flow test with in-line HPLC monitoring to detect gradual BPR pressure drift indicating fouling.
Perform mixing validation using a fast kinetic probe reaction at Q=0.56 mL/min to confirm enhanced laminar mixing meets selectivity targets.
Conduct pressure relief test: simulate BPR failure by manually venting to verify pump auto-shutdown and system depressurization within 5 seconds.
